disclaimer.title: Please review before using this app
disclaimer.intro: To keep using this app, you must agree to the following.
disclaimer.point1: This tool is for informational purposes only and is not investment advice.
disclaimer.point2: Price and exchange rate data may be inaccurate or delayed.
disclaimer.point3: You are solely responsible for your investment decisions and their outcomes.
disclaimer.point4: No data is stored on any server; everything stays in your browser only.
disclaimer.agree: I have read and agree to the above.
disclaimer.point5: Tax-credit and tax-free figures in the Tax Benefit Calculator are for reference only, not tax advice. Verify exact amounts via National Tax Service Hometax or a tax professional.
disclaimer.point6: This app may display ads (e.g. Kakao AdFit, Google AdSense) to help cover operating costs. Ad networks may use their own cookies for ad personalization, governed by each network's own privacy policy — this app itself never sends your portfolio data (holdings, allocations, etc.) to any ad network.

allocation.title: Target Asset Allocation
allocation.description: Define your target categories and weights. The total must equal 100%.
allocation.totalWarning: Weights must add up to exactly 100% before you can use the rebalance calculator.
allocation.copyHint: Copying replaces all of this account's existing categories with the selected account's categories. Holdings in a category with a matching name are automatically moved to the new category and kept, but holdings in a category with no matching name in the source account are deleted along with it.
allocation.copyConfirm: Replace this account's categories with those from "{source}"? All existing categories here will be deleted.
allocation.copyConfirmWithLoss: Replace this account's categories with those from "{source}"? All existing categories here will be deleted, and {count} holding(s) with nowhere to move to will be deleted along with them. This cannot be undone.
allocation.copyLossWarning: ⚠ {count} holding(s) in this account have no matching category and will be deleted.
allocation.modeHint: Choose Unified to follow the single shared target allocation used by every 'Unified' account (percentages can't be edited here — edit the shared allocation itself instead). Choose Individual to define and edit this account's own categories. New accounts default to Unified.
allocation.unifiedFollowNote: This account follows the unified allocation. The values below are currently in effect and can't be edited here — to change them, use "Edit unified allocation" below to edit the source.
allocation.unifiedEditorDescription: Changes here apply immediately to every account in Unified mode. Renaming a category doesn't break any account's holdings links (they're connected by a stable internal id — the name is just a display label). Deleting a category also deletes the holdings in every account that mirrors it, so you'll see how many accounts/holdings are affected before it happens.
allocation.unifiedEditorAppliesNote: The total above is for the unified allocation itself. It doesn't affect accounts switched to Individual mode.
allocation.unifiedRemoveConfirm: Delete category "{name}"? It will also be removed from every unified account that mirrors it.
allocation.unifiedRemoveConfirmWithLoss: Delete category "{name}"? {count} holding(s) across {accounts} account(s) that follow it will be deleted too. This can't be undone.

holdings.title: Holdings
holdings.description: Enter your current holdings. Current price can be entered manually or refreshed.
holdings.name: Name
holdings.fxError: Failed to fetch exchange rate (using fallback value)
holdings.fxSummaryDescription: Splits the KRW gain/loss into price movement and currency (FX) movement.
holdings.sellExceedsHolding: Cannot sell more than you currently hold.
holdings.groupedHint: Adding the same ticker again merges it automatically. Click a row to expand and view or edit individual buy/sell records.
holdings.moveToAccountCategory: Select to move this holding to a different account/category.
holdings.deleteLotConfirm: Delete this buy/sell entry? This cannot be undone.

calculator.title: Rebalance Calculator
calculator.description: Enter a deposit amount to calculate a buy allocation toward your targets.
calculator.noHoldings: Please set up holdings and allocation first.
calculator.invalidAllocation: Your target allocation doesn't add up to 100% yet. Fix it on the Target Allocation screen before calculating.
calculator.sellQuantityNote: Sell quantities are whole shares chosen to get as close as possible to the target amount (may not match exactly).
calculator.applyCostsInfo: On sells, shows the KR securities transaction tax (0.20%) for domestic stocks, or a reference capital gains tax estimate (22% of this sale's realized gain) for US stocks. Trading fees vary by broker/product and are not included here.
calculator.sourceTax: Source: Securities Transaction Tax Act Art. 8; Income Tax Act Art. 118-2 (foreign asset capital gains)
calculator.costNote: The US capital gains tax estimate is based only on this single sale; the actual tax owed depends on your full year's realized gains and the 2,500,000 KRW annual deduction, filed the following May. Check the History page for cumulative annual realized gains.
calculator.usCapitalGainsNote: This includes a US stock sale. The capital gains estimate is reference only, not tax advice.
calculator.unifiedHint: Combines holdings across all accounts, merging categories with the same name into one. Using consistent category names across accounts gives a more accurate result.
calculator.unifiedWarningTitle: Categories with the same name have different targets across accounts — using the average
calculator.unifiedMultiAccountNote: Split across accounts: {accounts} — execute the actual trade in whichever account you choose.
calculator.taxResidencyHint: Korea's securities transaction tax on KR-listed stock sales always applies regardless of your tax residency. Only capital gains tax rules depend on residency — KR residents are taxed 22% on foreign (US) stock gains only, while US residents/citizens must report worldwide gains (including KR-listed stock gains) to the IRS under the US worldwide-income taxation principle, since Korea's domestic-stock tax exemption for its own residents has no bearing on US filing obligations.
calculator.usSubjectToNiitLabel: Subject to Net Investment Income Tax (NIIT 3.8%)
calculator.usTaxSettingsNote: The long-term rate is estimated automatically from your filing status and taxable income (same logic as the US tab in the Tax Benefit Calculator). This calculator doesn't model the full US federal ordinary-income brackets, so enter your own marginal rate for the short-term rate. Holding period (long/short-term) is approximated from the quantity-weighted average purchase date of your buy lots.
calculator.costNoteUs: This US-residency capital gains estimate is based on this single sale only. Your actual tax liability depends on your other gains/losses for the year and your overall income. Yearly cumulative realized gains (split by long/short-term) are available on the Transaction History page.
calculator.usResidencyNote: Calculating under US tax residency. For KR-listed stock sales, an estimated US federal capital gains tax is shown alongside the KR securities transaction tax. This is not tax advice.
calculator.usdKrwRateInfo: This rate is used to convert KRW and USD holdings and your deposit amount into a single base currency (KRW) to calculate target percentages. The resulting buy/sell amounts are then converted back into each holding's original currency. It defaults to a live rate (Frankfurter.app); editing it overrides the live rate.

settings.title: Settings & Backup
settings.importWarning: Importing will overwrite your currently saved data.
settings.backupDescription: Export or import all your data — categories, holdings, watchlist, and asset trend history — as a single file. Nothing is sent to a server.
settings.importError: Import failed. Please check the backup file.

history.title: Transaction History
history.description: All buy/sell records across every holding, newest first. Same underlying data you can expand per ticker on the Holdings screen.
history.usGainsInfo: Realized gains from already-executed US stock sells, summed by year. Foreign stock capital gains tax is computed on the full year's combined gains rather than per transaction, so this helps you gauge whether you're over the 2,500,000 KRW annual deduction.
history.usGainsSource: Source: Income Tax Act Art. 118-2 et seq. (foreign asset capital gains), 2,500,000 KRW annual deduction, 22% rate (incl. local tax)
history.usGainsDescription: Only counts US stock sells in this account. If you have other general (taxable) accounts, add their realized gains too to check your actual filing threshold. Pension savings, IRP, and US tax-advantaged accounts follow different tax rules than this 22% rule.
history.usGainsDeductionNote: The first 2,500,000 KRW ({deduction} KRW) per year is tax-free. The KRW conversion uses today's rate, not the actual sale-date rate, so it may differ from the real filing amount.
history.usGainsApproximatedNote: * Entries without a recorded buy or sell FX rate were calculated using today's rate instead (may not be exact).
history.taxResidencyHint: Korea's securities transaction tax on KR-listed stock sales always applies regardless of your tax residency. Only capital gains tax rules depend on residency — KR residents are taxed 22% on foreign (US) stock gains only, while US residents/citizens must report worldwide gains (including KR-listed stock gains) to the IRS under the US worldwide-income taxation principle.
history.usResidentGainsInfo: Since the US taxes residents and citizens on worldwide income, this includes sales of both KR- and US-listed stocks. Long-term (held over 1 year) and short-term (1 year or less) gains are shown separately since they're taxed at different rates. Holding period is approximated from the number of days between the quantity-weighted average purchase date of the buy lots and the sale date (this app doesn't support selling specific lots).
history.usResidentGainsSource: Source: IRS Topic no. 409, Capital gains and losses
history.usResidentGainsDescription: Combines KR- and US-listed stock sales into yearly, long/short-term realized gain totals. The number in parentheses is the sell count.
history.usSubjectToNiitLabel: Subject to Net Investment Income Tax (NIIT 3.8%)
history.usResidentApproximatedNote: KR-listed (KRW) stock gains are converted to USD using the current exchange rate as an approximation (USD-listed stocks need no conversion).
history.usResidentRateNote: The long-term rate is auto-estimated ({rate}%) from your filing status and taxable income, adjustable on the US tab of the Tax Benefit Calculator. The short-term rate is what you entered. Actual tax may differ based on other gains/losses, state tax, and more — this is not tax advice.

trend.title: Monthly Asset Trend
trend.description: Automatically records today's total portfolio value each time you use the app, building a monthly trend over time. It only starts accumulating from today onward, since no historical price data is fetched.
trend.empty: No snapshots yet. Once you enter holdings and come back over the following days/months, a trend will appear here.
trend.onlyOneNote: Only one month of data so far — this is just the current value, not yet a trend. It will fill in over time.
trend.indexedNote: Since currency and scale differ, both series are indexed to 100 at the first comparable month and shown as relative returns.
trend.scopeAllAccountsHint: Sums each account's monthly value together. If an account wasn't opened in a given month, its snapshot for that month may be missing from the total.

risk.structuralDescription: Shows how concentrated your holdings are by ticker, category, currency, and market. This measures concentration in your current structure, not historical price volatility.
risk.noEtfHoldings: No holdings have been identified as ETFs yet (this is only known once fundamentals finish loading).
risk.hhiNote: HHI (Herfindahl-Hirschman Index) sums the squares of each weight. 1 means everything is in one holding/category; with n evenly-weighted holdings it equals 1/n. A red card means a common rule of thumb was exceeded (largest holding 20%, top 3 50%, holding HHI 0.25, category HHI 0.4) — these are not hard rules.
risk.grahamDescription: Automatically evaluates Benjamin Graham's defensive investor criteria from The Intelligent Investor for each individual stock. Green means it passes, red means it fails, gray (-) means there wasn't enough data. Hover the i icon next to each column for what it means and its source.
risk.grahamDataNote: Uses Yahoo Finance's free financial data. Some fields (especially for Korean tickers or newer listings) may be missing, and this is an unofficial API that can occasionally fail. Use ↻ to retry.
risk.etfDescription: An ETF isn't a company — it's a basket of assets — so the Graham checklist (built on financial statements) doesn't apply. Instead this looks at expense ratio, top-holdings concentration, and whether it's a leveraged/inverse product.
risk.etfDataNote: Once fundamentals finish loading and a holding is identified as an ETF, it automatically moves here from the stock table above. Same unofficial Yahoo Finance data, so some fields may be missing or fail.
risk.sourceGraham: Source: Benjamin Graham, The Intelligent Investor, ch. 14 (defensive investor criteria) · Data: Yahoo Finance (unofficial)
risk.sourceEtf: Source: common ETF risk factors (cost, concentration, leverage) · Data: Yahoo Finance (unofficial)
risk.check_marketCap: Whether the company is large enough. Graham's original threshold ($100M revenue, 1970s dollars) doesn't translate cleanly to today, so a $2B+ market cap (or KRW equivalent) is used as a modern approximation.
risk.check_currentRatio: Current assets / current liabilities — short-term ability to cover bills due within a year. Graham's threshold: at least 2x.
risk.check_debtToEquity: Debt / equity — how reliant the company is on borrowed money. Graham's original criterion was 'long-term debt should be less than net working capital', which isn't available for free, so debt/equity <= 1 is used as an approximation.
risk.check_earningsStability: Whether the company was profitable every year in the available data. Graham's threshold is 10 straight years; free data usually only covers about the last 4 years.
risk.check_earningsGrowth: Whether earnings have been trending up. Graham's threshold is at least 33% EPS growth over 10 years; with a shorter available window the target is scaled down proportionally (e.g. ~13% over 4 years).
risk.check_dividendRecord: Consecutive years with a dividend payment. Graham's threshold: 20+ uninterrupted years. Quality growth stocks that deliberately don't pay dividends will fail this one criterion.
risk.check_per: Price / earnings per share — how expensive the stock is relative to profit. Graham's threshold: 15x or less.
risk.check_pbr: Price / book value per share — how expensive the stock is relative to its balance-sheet net worth. Graham's threshold: 1.5x or less.
risk.check_perPbrCombo: P/E multiplied by P/B — Graham's combined alternative to the separate P/E and P/B tests. Passes at 22.5 or below.
risk.check_leverage: Estimated from the name/ticker containing terms like 2X, 3X, Ultra, or Inverse. These funds rebalance daily, so in volatile markets losses can compound faster than the underlying index moves (volatility decay).
risk.check_expenseRatio: The annual management fee taken automatically from fund assets. Lower is better for long-term returns. 0.5% or less is treated as low-cost (large index ETFs are typically 0.03-0.1%).
risk.check_concentration: Combined weight of the fund's top holdings. Despite the 'index fund' label, some ETFs are heavily weighted toward a handful of names, so 40% or less is treated as reasonably diversified.
risk.enterprisingDescription: The enterprising (aggressive) investor criteria from chapter 15 of the same book. The bar is lower than the defensive checklist, so more stocks qualify — but the tradeoff is that you're expected to dig in yourself. Reuses the same data as the defensive checklist above.
risk.sourceGrahamEnterprising: Source: Benjamin Graham, The Intelligent Investor, ch. 15 (enterprising investor criteria) · Data: Yahoo Finance (unofficial)
risk.echeck_currentRatio: Current assets / current liabilities. The enterprising threshold (1.5x) is looser than the defensive one (2x).
risk.echeck_debtToEquity: Debt / equity. Graham's original criterion was 'debt no more than 110% of net current assets', which isn't available for free, so debt/equity <= 1.5 (looser than the defensive 1.0) is used as an approximation.
risk.echeck_earningsStability: Whether the company was profitable every year in the available data. Graham's original threshold is 5 straight years (half of the defensive requirement); usually about 4 years of data is available.
risk.echeck_currentDividend: Whether the company is paying a dividend right now (unlike the defensive checklist, no 20-year streak is required).
risk.echeck_earningsGrowth: Whether the most recent year's earnings are higher than the oldest available year. Unlike the defensive checklist (33%+ over 10 years), there's no specific magnitude threshold.
risk.echeck_priceToTangibleAssets: Graham's original criterion is 'price no more than 120% of tangible asset value' (net assets excluding intangibles). Tangible-only book value isn't available for free, so regular price/book <= 1.2 is used as an approximation.
risk.fitDescription: Checks whether your holdings in this {accountType} account actually match its tax benefits and trading scope.
risk.fitDisclaimer: This check includes name-based heuristics (e.g. an ETF named "US" or "Bond" is assumed foreign/bond-type) and is for reference only — verify exact product classification in the prospectus.
risk.fitSource: Source: Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 91-18 (ISA); Enforcement Decree of the Financial Investment Services Act (derivative risky-asset limits); IRS Publication 590-A/B (US IRA general rules)
risk.finding_generalNoRestriction: A general account has no special tax benefits or trading restrictions — it can be managed freely.
risk.finding_foreignDirectStock: This is a stock listed directly on a foreign (US) exchange, which this account type cannot trade. It may actually be held in a different account, or the account assignment in this app may be incorrect.
risk.finding_isaTaxableEtfGood: This appears to be a product whose gains would normally be taxed (e.g. foreign-index or bond-type), so it makes good use of the ISA tax-free/reduced-rate benefit.
risk.finding_isaDomesticEtfLimited: This appears to track a domestic stock index, so its capital gains were likely already tax-free outside an ISA. The ISA-specific tax benefit may be limited here (dividends still benefit).
risk.finding_isaDividendGood: With a dividend yield of about {yield}%, this benefits from the ISA tax-free/reduced-rate treatment on dividend income, which is normally taxable.
risk.finding_isaLowBenefitStock: This is a domestic individual stock with a low dividend yield. Since its capital gains were already tax-free, holding it in an ISA may add little extra benefit.
risk.finding_pensionLeverageBanned: This appears to be a leveraged/inverse product. Pension savings and IRP accounts are fully prohibited from trading these, so this may not actually be tradeable, or the account assignment may be incorrect.
risk.finding_irpRiskyAssetLimitInfo: IRP accounts can only allocate up to 70% of the balance to risky assets (equity ETFs/funds, etc). This app doesn't track principal-guaranteed product balances, so verify the real ratio in your brokerage app.
risk.finding_usAccountKrListedStockCheck: This is a stock listed on a domestic (KR) exchange. Most US 401(k)/IRA accounts only support trading US-exchange-listed stocks/ETFs, not securities listed directly on foreign exchanges (this is a brokerage limitation, not a legal prohibition, and varies by broker). Check with your broker whether this holding is actually tradeable in this account.
risk.finding_usRothAfterTaxInfo: Roth IRA contributions are after-tax, and qualified withdrawals of both principal and earnings are tax-free. Check the annual contribution limit and income-based eligibility on the Tax Benefits page (US tab).
risk.finding_usTraditionalPreTaxInfo: Traditional IRA contributions may be tax-deductible (pre-tax effect), and withdrawals of both principal and earnings are taxed as ordinary income. The deductible amount can be reduced based on workplace-plan coverage and income (see the Tax Benefits page).
risk.finding_us401kInfo: 401(k) contributions are pre-tax payroll deductions by default; employer matching and vesting rules vary by plan. Check the annual contribution limit on the Tax Benefits page (US tab).

watchlist.title: Watchlist
watchlist.description: Track tickers you don’t hold yet — price and change only. Not included in rebalancing.
watchlist.name: Name

taxBenefits.title: Tax Benefit Calculator
taxBenefits.description: Estimate pension-account tax credits and ISA tax-free limits under currently effective Korean tax law.
taxBenefits.notAdviceWarning: This is reference information only, not tax advice. Actual results depend on your full income and deduction profile. Check the National Tax Service Hometax (year-end settlement preview) or a tax professional for exact figures. Proposed reforms that have not yet passed the National Assembly (e.g. a proposed higher ISA contribution cap) are not included.
taxBenefits.pensionInfo: Contributions to pension savings and IRP accounts, up to a set limit, qualify for a 13.2–16.5% tax credit on your annual income tax filing.
taxBenefits.totalSalaryPlaceholder: Leave blank if not a salaried employee
taxBenefits.isaTransferInfo: Transferring matured ISA funds into a pension account within 60 days adds 10% of the transferred amount (up to 3,000,000 KRW) to your tax-credit limit.
taxBenefits.pensionLimitNote: Pension savings alone caps at 6,000,000 KRW; combined with IRP the cap is {total} (excluding the ISA-transfer bonus).
taxBenefits.isaInfo: Net gains inside an ISA (interest, dividends, capital gains) are tax-free up to a limit, and taxed at a reduced 9.9% above it — lower than the standard 15.4% financial income tax.
taxBenefits.sourceNts: Source: National Tax Service, "Pension Account Tax Credit"; Income Tax Act Art. 59-3
taxBenefits.sourceIsa: Source: Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 91-18 (ISA tax treatment)

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.description: Keep target allocation and holdings fully separate per account — Korean accounts (pension savings, IRP, ISA), US accounts (401(k), Traditional/Roth IRA), or general. Deleting an account also deletes its allocation and holdings.
accounts.deleteWarning: This will delete "{name}" and all of its allocation and holdings. Continue?
accounts.lastAccountHint: At least one account must remain.

usTaxBenefits.notAdviceWarning: This is reference information only, not tax advice. Actual results depend on state taxes and your full income/deduction profile. Check the official IRS worksheets (Publication 590-A/B) or a tax professional for exact figures. All figures are for tax year 2026.
usTaxBenefits.contributionInfo: 401(k) plans (including 403(b)/457/TSP) and IRAs add an age-based catch-up contribution on top of the base limit. Ages 60-63 get a higher special catch-up.
usTaxBenefits.traditionalInfo: If neither you nor your spouse is covered by a workplace retirement plan, contributions are fully deductible regardless of income. If covered, the deductible amount phases out based on your MAGI.
usTaxBenefits.coveredByWorkplacePlan: I'm covered by a workplace retirement plan (e.g. 401(k))
usTaxBenefits.spouseCovered: My spouse is covered by a workplace plan (I'm not)
usTaxBenefits.rothInfo: Roth IRA contributions are after-tax, and qualified withdrawals are fully tax-free. Above a certain MAGI, the amount you can contribute is reduced or eliminated entirely.
usTaxBenefits.ltcgInfo: Gains on assets held over a year are taxed federally at 0%, 15%, or 20% based on taxable income. High earners may owe an additional 3.8% Net Investment Income Tax (NIIT).
usTaxBenefits.niitNote: Above certain thresholds (roughly $200k single / $250k married filing jointly), an additional 3.8% Net Investment Income Tax (NIIT) may apply on top of the rate above. NIIT is not included in this calculator.
usTaxBenefits.sourceIrs401k: Source: IRS, "401(k) limit increases to $24,500 for 2026, IRA limit increases to $7,500" (IR-2025-111)
usTaxBenefits.sourceIrsIra: Source: IRA/Roth IRA income phase-out guidance in the IRS release above (IR-2025-111); IRS Publication 590-A
usTaxBenefits.sourceIrsLtcg: Source: IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32 (2026 inflation adjustments)
